## Overview

The `BlankmanF` package provides tools for conducting and visualizing the Friedman test. This vignette introduces the main functions of the package with usage examples.

---

## Function: `run_friedman_test()`

```{r}
run_friedman_test <- function(data, subject_col, treatment_col, response_col) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(response_col, "~", treatment_col, "|", subject_col))
  result <- stats::friedman.test(formula, data = data)

  summary_table <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[treatment_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(Mean_Rank = mean(rank(-.data[[response_col]])), .groups = "drop")

  list(
    statistic = result$statistic,
    p_value = result$p.value,
    df = result$parameter,
    method = result$method,
    summary = summary_table
  )
}
```

---

## Function: `plot_friedman_ranks()`

```{r}
plot_friedman_ranks <- function(data, subject_col, treatment_col, response_col) {
  ranked_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[subject_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Rank = rank(-.data[[response_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  summary_ranks <- ranked_data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[treatment_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(Mean_Rank = mean(Rank), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot2::ggplot(summary_ranks, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[[treatment_col]], y = Mean_Rank)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Mean Ranks by Treatment", x = "Treatment", y = "Mean Rank") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
}
```

---

## Function: `get_friedman_summary()`

```{r}
get_friedman_summary <- function(data, subject_col, treatment_col, response_col) {
  ranked_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[subject_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Rank = rank(-.data[[response_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  ranked_data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[treatment_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      Mean_Rank = mean(Rank),
      SD_Rank = sd(Rank),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

## Example Data and Test

```{r}
example_data <- data.frame(
  Subject = rep(1:6, each = 3),
  Treatment = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), times = 6),
  Score = c(85, 88, 90, 78, 80, 82, 91, 93, 92, 87, 89, 90, 70, 72, 74, 76, 77, 79)
)

run_friedman_test(example_data, "Subject", "Treatment", "Score")
plot_friedman_ranks(example_data, "Subject", "Treatment", "Score")
get_friedman_summary(example_data, "Subject", "Treatment", "Score")
```
